title: trustdiff report, schema version 1
description: The document written by trustdiff --format json. Within schema version 1 fields are added, never renamed or removed; a breaking change bumps the version in the schema field and in this file's name.

schema.description: Identifies the document format. Always trustdiff.report/1 for documents that match this schema.

subjects.description: One entry per evaluated subject, in the order the run evaluated them: command line order for check, lockfile order for diff and scan. A lockfile that installs one version from two different places is two subjects, one per line, so a copy repointed at another archive is not hidden by a clean one.

tool.description: Build identity of the trustdiff binary that wrote the document.

version.description: Release tag such as v0.1.0, or dev for a build without link-time version information.

commit.description: Short git commit the binary was built from, or none.

date.description: Commit or build timestamp in RFC 3339, or unknown.

go_version.description: Go toolchain the binary was compiled with, for example go1.26.8.

policy.description: The settings that shaped the run after the command line flags and the policy file were reconciled.

path.description: Policy file that was loaded, as given or discovered. Empty when the built-in defaults were used.

cooldown.description: Threshold of the young-version check in the spelling the policy accepts, for example 3d, 12h, 1w or P3D. Per-ecosystem overrides are reported in the evidence of each finding.

fail_on.description: Lowest finding level that makes the exit code 1. never means the exit code is 0 whatever the findings are; exit codes 2 and 3 are unaffected.

ref.description: A package, optionally at one version, in one ecosystem. The textual form is ecosystem:name[@version].

ecosystem.description: Registry the package lives in. deno and jsr are accepted from milestone M4 on.

name.description: Package name in the registry's canonical spelling: exactly as npm and jsr spell it, because npm serves two names that differ only in case as two packages; PEP 503 normalized for pypi; the registered spelling for cargo, which allocates a name case-insensitively and treats - and _ as one character. Scoped npm and jsr names keep their @scope/ prefix.

version.description: The exact version the entry refers to. Present for every evaluated subject and finding; absent only when no version could be resolved.

location.description: Where a subject came from when it was read from a lockfile.

path.description: Lockfile path relative to the directory the run started in, with forward slashes.

line.description: One-based line of the entry in the lockfile. Absent when the parser could not attribute the entry to a line.

skipped.description: A check that could not run for a subject. Skips are reported, never hidden, so that an unavailable data source is not mistaken for a pass.

check.description: Id of the check that was skipped, for example TD012.

reason.description: Why the check did not run, in one sentence: an unavailable data source, offline mode, or a check that does not apply to the ecosystem.

finding.description: One result of one check for one package version. The id, name and evidence keys are stable within a schema version and documented per check in docs/checks.md.

id.description: Stable check identifier, for example TD002.

name.description: The check's policy name, for example publisher-changed.

level.description: Effective level after the policy was applied. Checks set to off produce no findings.

title.description: One line suitable for a terminal or a code scanning annotation.

explanation.description: The human account of the evidence, for example: previous 5 versions were published by alice; 4.19.3 was published by bob-ci.

evidence.description: Machine-readable facts behind the explanation. Keys are specific to each check and documented in docs/checks.md; absent when the check recorded none.

subject.description: One evaluated package version with everything the checks said about it.

direct.description: True when the subject is a direct dependency of the project. Absent means false.

evaluated.description: Ids of the checks that ran to completion for this subject, sorted. A check that ran and found nothing is listed here and has no finding.

skipped.description: Checks that could not run for this subject, sorted by check id.

findings.description: Findings sorted by level, most severe first, then by check id.

verdict.description: The highest finding level, or ok when every check that ran found nothing, or skipped when no check could be evaluated.

summary.description: Counts over all subjects and the process exit code, so a script needs nothing else.

findings.description: Number of findings per level over all subjects. Every key is present even when its count is zero.

skipped.description: Number of skipped checks over all subjects.

exit_code.description: The process exit code: 0 no finding at or above fail_on, 1 at least one finding at or above fail_on, 3 a required data source was unavailable and the policy says on_data_unavailable: fail. Exit code 2 (usage or configuration error) is never accompanied by a document.

exit_meaning.description: The exit code spelled out: no blocking findings, blocking findings, or a required data source was unavailable.
